name: Lifetime
label: Jade Tree
lede: A Michigan kid moved to New Jersey in 1989 just to start a band; seven years and about forty-five minutes of Jade Tree records later, half of emo's next decade was copying him.

eras.title: A Michigan kid comes east to start a band
eras.text: Dan Yemin moved from Michigan to New Jersey with one goal, and found a singer in Ari Katz of the local band Enuf. Their first version of Lifetime was a scrappy New Brunswick hardcore band whose one LP, Background, came out on New Age Records.

years.h: Dan Yemin moves from Michigan to New Jersey to start a band
years.p: Yemin later told Punknews the whole dream was modest: make something someone liked enough to put out a 7-inch.

years.h: [[Ari Katz|1eb933dd-96ff-4019-a07d-16c8cf34989f]] and [[Dan Yemin|bfac6050-54c5-4b29-bb73-465c90e6e327]] form Lifetime in New Brunswick
years.p: Katz came from the local band Enuf. Yemin says the name came from the second [[Rollins Band|3ca37f23-fdce-49ce-86e2-134c9a17ebc5]] album, Lifetime; Katz disputes that story.
years.xp:
Asked about the name sixteen years on, Dan Yemin credited the 1987 Rollins Band record. Ari Katz remembers it differently, and Yemin shrugged it off to Punknews: after that long, the two of them remember everything differently.

What they agreed on was the lyrical line. Katz steered away from the tough-guy violence of New York hardcore toward personal, positive songs, which became the band's signature.

years.h: Lifetime's first California shows make friends for life
years.p: Two women Dan Yemin met at those 1991 West Coast gigs stayed friends with the band and turned up at its 2005 reunion shows.

years.h: Background tracked at SRA Music Studio in Scotch Plains, New Jersey
years.p: The first lineup: Katz, Yemin, guitarist Scott Saint Hilaire, bassist Justin Janisch and drummer David Wagenschutz. Bonus live tracks came from Lost Horizons in Syracuse on July 5, 1992.

years.h: Background, New Age Records No. 15
years.p: Lifetime's debut LP came out on the California straight-edge label New Age. A European edition retitled Ghost was pressed in 1,000 copies by Break Even Point.
years.xp:
Nobody in the band was sentimental about it. When fans asked for Background songs at the reunion, Dan Yemin's reply to Punknews was a blunt question about whether they had ears.

Bassist Dave Palaitis later remixed the whole album for the 2006 Jade Tree set Somewhere in the Swamps of New Jersey, which pairs the remix with the original.

eras.title: Reinvented on Jade Tree
eras.text: With a rebuilt lineup and producer Steve Evetts, Lifetime cut two short, fast, hooky records for a young Delaware label called Jade Tree. Hello Bastards and Jersey's Best Dancers put love songs and Hüsker Dü melody inside hardcore, and the band broke up right after the second one.

years.h: Pete Martin, Dave Palaitis and Scott Golley join Lifetime
years.p: Guitarist Pete Martin, bassist Dave Palaitis and drummer Scott Golley complete the five-piece that plays on both Jade Tree albums.

years.h: Steve Evetts records Hello Bastards at Trax East, South River NJ
years.p: [[Steve Evetts|ae091a4c-0a25-4555-8874-5f05768d9d18]] produced and engineered the sessions at Trax East, the studio that would keep coming back into this story with [[Kid Dynamite|c5300096-cfb0-4801-b146-166e2d02f08a]].

years.h: Hello Bastards: 12 songs in 21 minutes on Jade Tree
years.p: Twelve songs, 21:37, including a cover of [[Hüsker Dü|5c4c90a4-539f-4101-83cf-301bc6a94e06]]'s It's Not Funny Anymore. Jade Tree still calls it one of the most influential punk albums of the decade.
years.xp:
Wikipedia lists the release as September 25, 1995; Lifetime's own Bandcamp says September 1. Either way it was early Jade Tree, a label run out of Wilmington, Delaware, and it gave the label its first real momentum.

Songs like (The Gym Is) Neutral Territory later landed on Vulture's list of the best emo songs ever, at No. 52, a tag the band itself never chased.

years.h: Glue Records collects Lifetime's 7-inches and outtakes
years.p: A compilation of the singles and unreleased songs came out on Glue Records in the US and on Day After Records in Europe.

years.h: Jersey's Best Dancers sessions begin at Trax East
years.p: Steve Evetts tracked the album in two bursts, June 1996 and January 1997, in the same South River studio.

years.h: Jersey's Best Dancers, the one everybody covers
years.p: Twenty-three minutes, and Pitchfork gave it 8.5. [[Fall Out Boy|516cef4d-0718-4007-9939-f9b38af3f784]] later covered Turnpike Gates, [[New Found Glory|6acb932e-840d-47ac-8e0d-725ad8a6e52c]] Cut the Tension and [[Rise Against|606bf117-494f-4864-891f-09d63ff6aa4b]] The Boy's No Good.
years.xp:
AllMusic called it a triumphant burst of upbeat punk rock, and it later showed up on best-of lists from Kerrang!, Rock Sound and Rolling Stone.

The bands who name Lifetime as a root reads like the next decade's Warped Tour bill: My Chemical Romance, Thursday, Saves the Day, Taking Back Sunday, Midtown and Senses Fail among them.

q: We were worrying too much about what other people thought.
years.h: Lifetime split in two over one big tour
years.p: After a short tour for Jersey's Best Dancers, Lifetime broke up in 1997. Dan Yemin says some members simply didn't want to tour anymore.
years.xp:
Yemin told Punknews that some members simply didn't want to tour anymore, and that the band divided into two camps over a major touring commitment.

He also admitted the band had drifted from the joy of it, worrying about outside opinion more than the music.

years.h: Dan Yemin and Dave Wagenschutz start [[Kid Dynamite|c5300096-cfb0-4801-b146-166e2d02f08a]] in Philadelphia
years.p: Yemin took the speed and melody straight into a new Philly band with former Lifetime drummer Dave Wagenschutz.

eras.title: Hellfest dies, Lifetime doesn't
eras.text: A one-off festival reunion collapsed at the last minute, so the band booked its own shows instead, and liked it enough to stay. Within a year Lifetime had a reissue on Jade Tree and a deal with Pete Wentz's label.

years.h: Hellfest is cancelled, so Lifetime books three shows of its own
years.p: The band was due at Hellfest on August 20, 2005. When it collapsed, Lifetime played the Trocadero in Philadelphia, the Starlight Ballroom, and the Stone Pony in Asbury Park with [[The Bouncing Souls|429d5f26-329c-41cc-bdff-17c29dbf1fb8]].
years.xp:
The Trocadero night on August 19 also brought back [[108|7f0c252a-bd45-4fe0-b306-478eeb07b97b]]. The Stone Pony show on August 21 added The Loved Ones, and its profits went to New Labor, The OUT Fund, the Nature Conservancy and Linda Ann's Greyhound Rescue.

Yemin told Punknews a Philadelphia show sold out a 1,200-person room online in about four minutes, and that Lifetime keeps no barricade: if kids get on stage, it's a party.

years.h: Lifetime announces it's back for real, not for one night
years.p: The band's statement said it would play again not as the resurrected corpse of a one-off reunion, but as friends who love making music.

years.h: Lifetime's reunion reaches California: Troubadour, Chain Reaction, Slims
years.p: Three West Coast nights in Los Angeles, Anaheim and San Francisco, fifteen years after the band's first California trip.

years.h: Free Lifetime show at SXSW in Austin
years.p: Donations from the South by Southwest show went to breast cancer research through Shirts for a Cure.

years.h: Somewhere in the Swamps of New Jersey on Jade Tree
years.p: A double-disc set of singles, comp tracks, covers and demos, plus Background twice: Dave Palaitis's remix and the original. The book has 52 pages and 40-plus rare photos.

years.h: Lifetime signs to Pete Wentz's Decaydance
years.p: The New Jersey hardcore band landed on the Fueled by Ramen imprint run by [[Fall Out Boy|516cef4d-0718-4007-9939-f9b38af3f784]]'s [[Pete Wentz|26cea341-dfab-483f-9cdb-8de82da81019]], one of the kids its records had raised.

eras.title: A new record, then free agents
eras.text: Lifetime made its first album in ten years with the same producer in the same studio, then walked away from Fueled by Ramen. The members kept busy in other bands while the old records kept getting reissued and covered.

years.h: Lifetime: back at Trax East with Steve Evetts
years.p: Recorded in fall 2006 in South River and done in 21:30. Punknews named it the No. 2 release of 2007; Pitchfork gave it 7.9.

years.h: Lifetime leaves Fueled by Ramen and becomes free agents
years.p: Punknews reported the split in January 2009, less than two years after the self-titled album.

years.h: Opening two shows for The Bouncing Souls
years.p: Lifetime supported fellow New Jersey lifers [[The Bouncing Souls|429d5f26-329c-41cc-bdff-17c29dbf1fb8]] for two dates in August 2009.

years.h: No Idea reissues Hello Bastards on colored vinyl
years.p: The Gainesville label pressed Hello Bastards on 12-inch in white, purple and green variants.

years.h: Lifetime says it's writing its first new music in 14 years
years.p: Brooklyn Vegan picked up the band's Facebook update. Members had spent the gap in [[Paint It Black|90910a44-7579-4730-9499-0546159fe4e3]], Beach Rats and Open City.
